title: Re-found broker completion on Job-empty so drained() cannot deadlock on the broker's own pipe copies
description:
Successor to task-7ba898f5 (nonblocking control polling), split out by governor ruling 2026-08-16 01:00Z with the human's standing unblock authorization. worker-dd806f63's measured findings (Serena: gotcha-broker-completed-is-gated-on-parent-teardown, task-task-7ba898f5...-handoff):

THE DEADLOCK. packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/broker/src/settle.rs:113-123 `fn drained<B: ByteChannel>` calls blocking `channel.read(&mut scratch)` and returns true only on `Ok(0)`; settle.rs:88-98 gates `Completion::Completed` on BOTH stdout/stderr drains, else `Completion::Unknown(Unobserved::ProviderEof)`. On a real Windows stdio pipe the broker holds its own fd4/fd5 write-end copies, so child exit never produces EOF — EOF arrives only when the NODE PARENT closes its endpoint (windows-boundary-session.ts:183-198 via windows-broker-process.ts:99-103, cancel/timeout/close only; onCompleted passes closeChannels=false). Measured: child gone ~200ms, boundary.completed at ~timeoutMs (6017ms for 6000, ~2000 for 2000). Through launchClaude, boundary-cancel and launcher-TIMEOUT coincide, closeProviderChannels destroys both captures, and the public result is CLAUDE_LAUNCH_STREAM_ERROR@OUTPUT.

REQUIRED DIRECTION (worker-validated; both naive halves fail alone): re-found the drain precondition on `wait_until_job_is_empty` — the Job-empty proof already guarantees zero live processes can hold a write end, so the post-Job-empty drain is bounded. Merely swapping drained() to poll_read yields Pending forever; merely closing the broker's fd copies after CreateProcess makes the broker's own drain unreadable. A never-ending provider must STILL reach Unobserved::ProviderEof. This is a semantic change to the completion contract — the architect must plan it as such, including which of settle.rs / session.rs / completion.rs it owns.

ACCEPTANCE ANCHOR: with this landed plus 7ba's delivered polling layer, the public launcher returns PROVEN (not TIMEOUT-coupled STREAM_ERROR) for a provider that outlives the 50ms slice and exits naturally, completion time tracking the CHILD (~hundreds of ms), not the configured timeout. The formerly-red untracked claude-launcher.windows.test.ts case "stays alive beyond the control poll slice" is the live repro — adopt or supersede it explicitly.

Task-7ba898f5 completes independently on its fd0/polling half; its DoD 1 natural-exit-PROVEN clause is explicitly re-scoped HERE (recorded in 7ba's status reason). task-6cbff010's Windows prerequisite chain is satisfied only when BOTH tasks are DONE — its architect must name both ids at re-measurement.
definitionOfDone: A real-Windows test proves the public launcher returns PROVEN for a provider that outlives the 50ms slice and exits naturally, with completion latency bounded by child exit (assert an explicit literal bound well under the configured timeout), not by timeoutMs.
A never-ending provider still reaches Unobserved::ProviderEof / its mapped stable refusal — the re-founding must not convert the old deadlock into a hang or a fail-open success.

The drain precondition is anchored on the Job-empty proof: a test (or drill) shows the drain runs only after wait_until_job_is_empty succeeds, and a mutation restoring the blocking pre-Job-empty drain turns a NAMED test red.
The formerly-red claude-launcher.windows.test.ts repro case ("stays alive beyond the control poll slice") is green, adopted into tracked tests or explicitly superseded by an equivalent named case.
Broker suite stays green on real Windows with nonzero executed counts; each gate leg's exit code read separately; foreign red disclosed verbatim under the path-attributed baseline rail.
taskRails: Semantic change to the completion contract: plan it explicitly — name every owned file among settle.rs/session.rs/completion.rs plus tests, and verify 7ba's landed polling layer (frames.rs, frames/polling.rs, boundary.rs, watch.rs) is consumed, not reworked.
Fail closed: absence of Job-empty proof or an unreadable drain must map to a stable Unknown/refusal code, never to Completed.
Re-measure settle.rs:88-123 and the TS boundary sites on current bytes before planning — shared worktree, claims above were measured 2026-08-16 00:53Z.
Preserve foreign work; commit only explicit owned paths.

THE REFUTED DESIGN, so you recognise it: "after Job-empty, treat `Pending` as drained." It is WRONG and was measured wrong. fd4/fd5 are DUPLEX handles and are the SAME handles the broker hands the child as stdout/stderr (main.rs:107-118 — `values[4]`/`values[5]` appear both in `Wiring` and in `inherited`). The child's writes travel toward NODE's end, so `drained()` reads the direction only Node writes, and Node never writes there. `wait_until_job_is_empty` licenses nothing about it because THE NODE PARENT IS NOT IN THE JOB. `drained()` is not late — it is structurally incapable of observing provider EOF.
Confirm the empirical proof rather than the code reading, because it is the decisive one: in worker-5678886b's candidate run the drain returned on the FIRST poll with ZERO bytes available while the launcher still captured byte-exact stdout AND stderr. `drained()` DISCARDS what it reads — had the broker been reading the child's output direction, those bytes would have been eaten and the capture empty. Re-read msg-5c7814a1 in #general and Serena `gotcha-broker-completed-is-gated-on-parent-teardown` for the numbers (HEAD 1000ms->1488ms, 2500ms->2996ms tracking the timeout; candidate 1180ms/1097ms flat, child-driven).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) THE REFUTED CANDIDATE — `drained()` on `poll_read` with `Pending => true`. Six lines, closes DoD 1, full broker suite 95/95, measured PROVEN and child-driven. REJECTED, and worker-5678886b was right not to land it: it inverts settle.rs:105-108's documented fail-closed line ("Running out of reads returns false, so the result stays UNKNOWN rather than being upgraded to an end nothing observed") and makes the precondition VACUOUS in production rather than re-founded. Its green depends on reading "no bytes right now" as "ended" — on a direction that never carries bytes at all. A precondition that always passes is worse than no precondition, because it still claims to be checking something.

2) OPTION (b) — broker drops its own fd4/fd5 copies after CreateProcess so the precondition means something. REJECTED after measuring the handle topology: fd4/fd5 are ONE duplex handle each, shared as the child's stdio. Dropping the broker's copy removes its only handle, so the drain then reads a closed handle — the failure already recorded in `gotcha-broker-completed-is-gated-on-parent-teardown`. Splitting the directions needs `DuplicateHandle`, which does NOT exist in the core crate, plus a Node-side pipe-creation change in windows-broker-process.ts. Cross-language, touches descriptor ownership, and lands squarely in the 7ba collision set — a large risky diff to preserve an observation the broker has no business making.

3) OPTION (c) — split again: land 7ba's fd0 half, narrow DoD 1, open another prerequisite. REJECTED: 7ba already completes independently on its own half and THIS task is the settle-side prerequisite that (c) would open. Splitting here defers the same decision a third time.

4) CHOSEN — (a)-with-deletion. Remove `Precondition::ProviderEof` and `Unobserved::ProviderEof` outright; `wait_until_job_is_empty` carries termination explicitly. Same observable outcome as the candidate, with no fail-open reading, and it is honest about what the broker can and cannot see. The vocabulary types force every consumer to be updated, and the change is provably Rust-internal.

5) Keep the precondition but document it as advisory. REJECTED: an observation that cannot be made is not advisory, it is decorative, and epic rail 4 is explicit that unverifiable evidence never gains authority. Deleting it is the only form that cannot be misread later.
